I've used Microsoft Office my whole life. If I switch to LibreOffice, what will I miss from Microsoft Office? Particularly Word.

The only issues I have ever encountered with it revolved around compatibility with PowerPoint presentations. Opening a PPP made in Office with Libre would cause formatting errors (or to crash), while opening something in Office made with Libre would cause formatting issues. Other than that, I have experience few problems. It is a robust and comfortable to use program. Plus it is a lot cheaper, especially since Microsoft is pushing that rental bullshit with Office365. Best thing is to understand what programs you use and what programs those you work with use, so that you can limit compatibility problems.

How do their spreadsheets compare to excel in terms of power and functionality? Excel is the only reason I'm on office, there's nothing like it as far as Financial Analysis tools, how does Libre compare?

In my experience, they are very similar in both functionality and ease of use. Best I can say it to try it and see. If you encounter any issues finding the tools you need, LibreOffice has some great, and very straight forward documentation. I think some of the biggest differences are in naming conventions, but even those are pretty similar and the ones that aren't are ease to learn.

It takes some getting used to the different ways they work, especially with formulas, but after that not so bad to switch as needed. I only switched back to MS Office because some proprietary software wouldn't import xls files made from OpenOffice. This was before Libre Office split off.

I use Excel and Calc (the LO equivalent) heavily and while they are pretty comparable they're not by any means exact copies of each other. The basics are pretty much the same but you may have to do some digging and get used to different syntax for some functionality.

If I'm helping someone at work, tend to use LibreOffice to open Word files that Word for some reason can't open up properly, then re-save it as a corrected Word file so they can use it.

My stuff is all in .odt, of course.

For a lot of research and paper stuff I use the .RTF format. I think it is one of the most universally compatible extensions, which limits compatibility issues, and the possibility of formatting problems. It might not have all the bells and whistles, but it gets the job done and limits many potential problems. I use .ODT for a lot of personal stuff. Although, if I plan on interchanging with Office I will use one of their formats.
Windows comes by default with WordPad, which can handle Rich Text Format! and it is 100% free. Does that have anything to do with your use of rich text?
